title: Long E Teams
kidRule: The long E sound is often spelled EE or EA. They sound exactly the same, so picture the word in your head to pick the right team! (Watch out: in a few words, like bread, EA says a short E instead.)
hint: Listen for the long E sound. Two vowels team up to make it. Can you picture which pair this word uses?
reminder: The long E sound here is spelled with a two-letter team: E-E or E-A.

check.question: Why do we write two E's in BETWEEN?
check.correctAnswer: Two E's together team up to say the long E sound!
distractors: Because the second E is silent and says nothing at all
Because every word needs two of the same vowel

words.def: In the middle of two things.
words.sent: The cat squeezed between the two fences.
words.story: Our planet Earth travels around the Sun between two neighbors, Venus and Mars!
words.card: *We* found a penguin hiding *between* the couch cushions!

words.def: One of the four parts of the year: spring, summer, fall, and winter.
words.sent: Fall is my favorite season because of the colorful leaves.
words.story: When it is summer in the United States, it is winter in Australia, because the two halves of the Earth take turns leaning toward the Sun!
words.card: My *son* the snowman says winter is the best *season*!

words.def: A person who helps you learn new things at school.
words.sent: Our teacher read us a funny story.
words.story: World Teachers' Day is celebrated all around the globe every year on October 5!
words.card: Our *teacher* gave *each* goldfish a gold star!

words.def: To say or do something again.
words.sent: Could you repeat the question, please?
words.story: Some parrots can repeat hundreds of words, and an African grey parrot named Alex even learned to name colors and shapes!
words.card: The parrot will *repeat* '*pea* soup' until you give him some!

words.def: The part of a shirt or coat that covers your arm.
words.sent: He wiped his nose on his sleeve.
words.story: Hundreds of years ago, sleeves were often made as separate pieces and tied or pinned onto a dress, so you could swap them!
words.card: On the *eve* of my birthday, a mouse moved into my *sleeve*!

words.def: A unit for measuring how hot or cold something is, or how wide an angle is.
words.sent: It got one degree warmer every hour.
words.story: A full circle has 360 degrees, an idea that goes back to the ancient Babylonians, who liked to count in sixties!
words.card: It is one *degree* outside, so the frog turned *gree*n and hopped back to bed!

words.def: To blow air out of your nose and mouth suddenly, with a loud achoo.
words.sent: Dust in the air made me sneeze.
words.story: Some people sneeze whenever they step into bright sunlight!
words.card: My k*nee* shook when I heard the giant *sneeze*!

words.def: A furry animal with a flat tail that builds dams in rivers.
words.sent: The beaver dragged a branch to its dam.
words.story: A beaver's front teeth are orange, and they never stop growing!
words.card: I want to *be* a *beaver* and build a fort out of popsicle sticks!

words.def: Under something or lower than it.
words.sent: The treasure was buried beneath the old oak tree.
words.story: Beneath the thick ice of Antarctica there are hundreds of hidden lakes of liquid water!
words.card: It is so *neat* that a troll keeps his socks *beneath* the bridge!

words.def: A clever African ape with dark hair and no tail.
words.sent: The chimpanzee used a stick to fish for termites.
words.story: Chimpanzees make tools! They poke sticks into termite mounds and pull them out covered with snacks.
words.card: The *chimpanzee* flipped a pancake so high that the *pan* is still waiting!
